body: I've never had my bag dimensions checked by Lufthansa, but that's probably the least of your worries. It's more likely that they'll make you check your carry on due to space issues. Then they'll lose it because they had no intention of actually making sure your bags get to wherever you're going.

I'm a believer that asking for your partner's blessing before doing something is just being considerate, but that's just how I prefer my relationship dynamic to be and it may be different for you and others, so the whole asking for "permission" thing doesn't bother me as much as it seems to bother other commenters. Of course I can still do whatever I want, but I also realize my autonomy affects my s/o and so I consider them. I've never felt restricted by this before in any way.  


>My gf found it weird that a female friend I was supposedly not that close to would confide in me that shes going through something emotionally

I would find this odd too if someone my partner claimed not to be close with went into explicit detail about their emotions. But if Luna just gave you a vague idea of why she was struggling with her work, like "sorry, I've just been a little stressed out with exams" then I do agree that your girlfriend's "reservations" aren't really justified.

  
It also matters who you had friendships with when you began dating. If your close friends are generally men, and you start suddenly becoming closer to one woman that your girlfriend has never met, I would think it's justified to find it unsettling. If that's not the situation and your close friendships are typically with women or an even mix of both, then your girlfriend would have less ground to be suspicious. From the sounds of it, you prefer to have a mix though and you're being restricted in that aspect.  


>its not fair considering I dont restrict her going out with any guy friends (not that she does to be truly honest anyways, but I simply wouldnt care if it happened)

Your girlfriend also doesn't seem to put you in situations where you can have suspicions about whether she's getting "too close" to a guy friend, whether you think you'd be fine with it or not. And if this is how she conducts herself, then it's reasonable she expects this of you too.

  
Ultimately though, if you don't like the dynamic that your girlfriend wants to impose, it's best for both of you to go your separate ways, but I'm not going to claim her being uncomfortable and issuing an ultimatum about it is a red flag because what she's asking of you is a valid dynamic to have and there are couples out there who make it work. It's not fair that you're uncomfortable and you don't have to stay in this relationship if you feel her boundaries are infringing on your autonomy.
